out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: 1) lettuce and tomatoes for sandwiches
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. STAFF DISCARDED THE FOOD. USE GLOVED HANDS OR UTENSILS TO HANDLE READY-TO-EAT FOODS.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Paper towels were not observed at the bar hand sink
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. PIC PLACED PAPER TOWELS AT THIS HAND SINK.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Shellstock Label Marked, Last Date Served/Sold Info
violations.observation: The date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served was observed recorded on the tag. Dates were observed either heavily smudged or illegible.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT THE DATE MUST BE LEGIBLE. EHS PROVIDED SHELL STOCK TAG GUIDANCE TO PIC.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: 1) Raw salmon burger was observed being stored above cooked chicken wings and dressings.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC MOVED THE RAW SALMON BURGER TO THE COOLER WITH RAW PROTEINS

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) in the 2DR prep top, fryer cooler: pickled red onions (46f), sour cream (46f), ranch (46f)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED THE AFOREMENTIONED FOODS.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: 1) utensils were observed being stored in a container of hot water on the stove. Hot water was observed at 103f
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC TO NOT STORE IN-USE UTENSILS IN WATER THAT IS UNDER 135f.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed that clean dishes being stored next to a handsink that is subjected to splash.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC TO MOVE CLEAN DISHES TO A CLEAN, DRY LOCATION.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Hand soap was not observed available at the bar hand sink
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. MANAGEMENT REFILLED THE HAND SOAP.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: 1) pickled red onions; 2) pickled peppers; 3) Orange tahini sauce; 4) cheese sauce
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. MANAGEMENT DISCARDED THE FOOD.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed no hand soap at the hand sink at the salad station.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. PIC PLACED MORE SOAP AT THE HAND SINK. MAKERS UNION (Inspection Date: 04/09/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Shellstock Label Marked, Last Date Served/Sold Info
violations.observation: The date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served is not recorded on the tag or label. EHS observed shellstock tags without the last sold date written on it.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC THAT ALL SHELLSTOCK TAGS MUST HAVE THE DATE IN WHICH THE LAST PIECE WAS SOLD WRITTEN ON THE TAG. RETAIN ALL THE TAGS WITHIN THE LAST 90 DAYS. PIC MAY DISCARD ANY TAG THAT ARE OLDER THAN 90 DAYS.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: EHS observed Raw salmon and Raw halibut being stored over bread and cooked pasta in the 2DR prep top cool across from the stove.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO MOVE ALL THE RAW FISH TO THE BOTTOM SHELF TO PREVENT CROSS CONTAMINATION. PIC MOVED RAW FISH TO THE BOTTOM SHELF.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) large squeeze bottle of Ranch (72f) in the 2DR prep top fry station); 2) pico de gallo (48f) and cut tomatoes (55f) in the 3DR prep top salad station.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED THE AFOREMENTIONED FOODS. TO ENSURE THE FOOD STAYS AT 41f OR COLDER, CLOSE THE PREP TOP LID DURING SLOW BUSINESS TIMES.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squeeze bottles of white wine, oils, and other liquids on the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC LABELED ALL THE SQUEEZE BOTTLES.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Linens & Napkins, Proper Use
violations.observation: EHS observed linens and towels being used in salad containers in the 3DR prep top cooler at the salad station.
violations.corrective_action: Linens may not be used in contact with food unless they are used to line a container for the service of foods and the linens are replaced each time the container is refilled for a new consumer. PIC REMOVED THE LINENS AND INSTRUCTED STAFF TO REWASH THE CUT GREENS.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: 1) spatulas and tongs being stored in a container of sanitizer on the cook line; 2) deli containers being stored in the bulk bins of seasoned flour and rice.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC REMOVED ALL OF THE IN-USE UTENSILS. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC ABOUT THE PROPER WAYS TO STORE UTENSILS.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. EHS observed employees handling raw fish changing gloves and switching tasks without washing hands.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS spoke to PIc and employees about issue, employee washed hands

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: EHS observed unsalted butter and breading station being stored on a counter without a 4 hr time marking
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. EHS spoke to PIC about issue. Provided timemark.
